subject: Pin authority delegation and transient-egress proof request
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Delegation of pin authority + transient egress proof for DPA

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare our DPA annex I need two things clarified before legal can sign:

1) Delegation / authority model: Acme's security team wants confirmation whether Redwood can accept a customer-specified operator (our security vendor) to trigger short-term cross-region hops for incident response. Essentially they want to delegate a limited "pin override" authority to a named operator for up to 72 hours in emergency scenarios. Is Redwood able to support a delegated operator identity model in the DPA (we would list the operator by name and AAD/ID)?

2) Transient egress proof: Legal wants artifact-level proof that any temporary cross-region processing will be logged and that KMS keys remain bound to the customer region except for a short, auditable window. Specifically we need:
  - an example audit log entry (redacted) showing a transient hop event,
  - the subprocessor roster versioning that would be active in the window, and
  - a statement on KMS-derived key handling during a transient hop.

Attached is the Acme DPA checklist and our mutual action plan template. Can you let me know what you can commit to and whether Redwood has a standard clause for "delegated pin-operator" semantics? If you prefer, we can sign a limited-scope addendum naming the operator.

Thanks — we are trying to close legal review this week if possible.

Best,
Priya
Priya Singh
Data Protection Officer, Acme Health
[Attachment: acme_dpa_checklist.pdf (PDF, 64KB)]
[Attachment: MAP-Acme-Health.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Delegation of pin authority + transient egress proof for DPA

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front:
- Delegated pin-operator: yes, we can support naming a delegated operator in an addendum with constrained permissions and time-bounded activation.
- Transient egress proof: we can provide redacted sample audit log entries and a short residency statement that describes KMS handling and the conditions under which a transient hop occurs.

I will loop in our legal and product folks to draft conservative language and collect the artifacts. Expect a proposed residency statement and a sample log extract from us by tomorrow.

Couple of notes for your legal team to be aware of:
- Our model ties ephemeral operator calls to a sealed audit trail and an approval token that records the initiating identity and TTL.
- KMS: customer-managed keys remain region-anchored; when a transient hop occurs we use an envelope key approach and we write an auditable TLS-protected token exchange to the audit log — we can document this in plain language for the DPA.

Attaching high-level plan (small stub) for the artifacts we will share.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Jonas —

I've pulled the roster and a redacted log example. High-level:
- Subprocessor roster (v2027-03-30) includes our infra partners and the specific edge caching vendor Acme flagged; I'll export a redacted CSV column set (company, purpose, region, effective_from).
- Audit log snippet: we have a sample entry for a transient hop (redacted IPs and account ids) with fields: event_id, initiator_id, operator_token_id, source_region, dest_region, start_ts, end_ts, reason_code, auditable_link. I'll redact PII and include it as a log sample.
- KMS note: for transient hops we use an envelope approach where customer CMKs are not exported; an ephemeral wrapping key is used and recorded in the audit entry. The residency statement will call this out in plain language.

Proposed DPA addendum language (first pass) for a delegated operator:  
"Customer and Redwood may mutually designate a named third-party operator with time-limited authorization (not to exceed 72 hours per incident) to initiate temporary cross-region processing for incident response. Any activation must be pre-authorized via the account's designated control plane and will generate an immutable audit trail recording identity, scope and TTL. Temporary processing does not include export of customer CMKs; any envelope key usage will be recorded and retained per the DPA's audit retention schedule."

Does this look conservative enough? If yes I'll produce the redacted artifacts and draft the residency statement PDF.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
